forms.name: bench-matrix
forms.question: How do these models compare across many benchmarks at once?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing a handful of models across many named benchmarks in one glance, especially when one model is the protagonist.
forms.antiUse: Trends over time or more than ~6 models — use a time-series form or a ranking board instead of a wide table.
forms.props: models (id, label, vendor?, color?, hero? — hero color must be a 6-digit hex, tint is built by hex+alpha concat), groups (label + rows {bench, note?, values: (number|null)[], decimals?}), meta?, footnote?, decimals?=1, benchColLabel?='benchmark'

forms.name: bubble-field
forms.question: How is the pool scattered across two axes?
forms.whenToUse: Showing how a pool of entities spreads across two quantitative axes with size and category as secondary encodings.
forms.antiUse: Few points with runs per entity and an efficiency story — use frontier-board; exact value reading — use a table.
forms.props: points: {x, y, size, category, label?}[]; categories: {key, label, color?}[]; xLabel; yLabel; xLog?; yLog?; width?; height?

forms.name: delta-bars
forms.question: Who is ahead today, and by how much?
forms.whenToUse: Tracking the day-by-day lead between exactly two rivals where the sign and streaks of the gap matter more than absolute volumes (head-to-head races, A/B momentum).
forms.antiUse: Not for more than 2 rivals or for absolute magnitudes — use race lines or stacked forms instead.
forms.props: a, b: {label, color?, values: (number|null)[]} (colors default to seriesColor(0)/seriesColor(1)); xLabels?: {frac, text}[]

forms.name: dumbbell-range
forms.question: How far apart are the two values per row, and who sits where?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing a two-point range across a handful of named entities where both endpoints and the gap matter (price min/max, input/output cost, before/after scores).
forms.antiUse: Not for more than 2 points per row (use a range strip or box plot) and not for time series — use lines.
forms.props: rows: {label, lo, hi, highlight?}[]; maxValue?; unit? (default "$"); formatValue?; loLabel?/hiLabel? (legend, default "lo"/"hi"); caption?; loColor? (default seriesColor(0)); hiColor? (default seriesColor(5)); highlightColor? (default seriesColor(1))
forms.example:

forms.name: dune-flow
forms.question: What made up the flow over time, and when were the waves?
forms.whenToUse: Daily composition of a volume stream (issues by priority, requests by tier) where the trend shape matters more than exact per-day spikes.
forms.antiUse: When readers must read exact values off the chart — the B-spline deliberately does not pass through the data points (raw values live only in the tooltip).
forms.props: days: ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'[] (min 4); series: { label, color?, values: (number|null)[] }[] stacked bottom-up; yLabel?: string

forms.name: frontier-board
forms.question: Which model delivers the most score per dollar (or token), and at what effort level?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing models on a quality-vs-cost tradeoff when each model has multiple runs (effort levels / modes) that form a frontier.
forms.antiUse: Needs >=2 runs per model to draw frontier lines; single-point-per-model data reads better as rank-bars.
forms.props: title, versions[] (datasets of models with runs), metrics[] (X-axis toggles with tickPrefix/Suffix), yMax/yTickSuffix, xAscending (two axis genres: default false = inverted, cheaper right, efficient corner up-right; true = conventional ascending, expensive right, efficient corner up-left), subjectId highlight, UI label strings

forms.name: heat-strip
forms.question: Is this thing alive — how did its activity move over the last year?
forms.whenToUse: Liveness at a glance over a long window of weekly counts (repo activity, releases, posts) where the shape and recency matter more than exact values.
forms.antiUse: Not for exact value reading or short ranges (<12 weeks) — use a column chart instead.
forms.props: weeks: number[] (weekly counts, oldest first, newest last); color? (default var(--vz-good,#059669))

forms.name: leaderboard-bars
forms.question: Who clears the bar, with what spread, and at what cost?
forms.whenToUse: Benchmark leaderboards where run-to-run spread (±std) and secondary costs (price/tokens/time) matter alongside the score; reference rows out of competition.
forms.antiUse: Single-metric rankings without spread or metric columns — use rank-bars; past ~12 rows the board outgrows a screen and labels stop scanning — use leaderboard-table.
forms.props: rows: {label, sub? (per-row note), value, std?, valueLabel?, color? (entity identity; default neutral), metrics?, offside?, offsideTag?}[]; columns?; barLabel?; rowLabel?; max?; unit?; ticks?

forms.name: leaderboard-table
forms.question: Who leads on score, with what confidence spread, and what does that score cost?
forms.whenToUse: Benchmark leaderboards where score alone is not enough: each run carries a spread (std) and economy metrics, and models have multiple effort levels worth comparing.
forms.antiUse: Wide-figure genre (min-width ~700px) — not for narrow containers or mobile cards; for a single metric without spread or economy columns, rank-bars is lighter.
forms.props: versions: {key, label, models: {id, color?, badge?, logoUrl?, runs: {variant?, score, std?, x}[]}[]}[] (same rail as frontier-board); columns: {key, label, prefix?, suffix?, decimals?}[]; meta?; footnote?; xMax?; scoreSuffix/scoreLabel/modelColLabel/bestLabel/allRunsLabel/modelsLabel/allLabel UI strings

forms.name: paired-bars
forms.question: How do two measurements of the same subjects compare?
forms.whenToUse: The same subjects measured two ways (two harnesses, two environments, two setups, plan vs fact) where per-subject deltas matter.
forms.antiUse: More than two measurements per subject — use a table or bench-matrix; two rivals over time — use delta-bars.
forms.props: groups: {label, color?, a: {label, value, valueLabel?}, b: {label, value, valueLabel?}}[]; max?; unit?; ticks?; barLabel?

forms.name: rank-bars
forms.question: Who leads this ranking, and by how much?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing one metric across a handful of named entities where order and gaps matter (leaderboards, price ladders).
forms.antiUse: Not for time series, part-to-whole composition, or more than ~10 rows — use a table or sparklines instead.
forms.props: items: {label, value, valueLabel?, sub?, highlight?, color?}[]; maxValue?; unit?; highlightColor? (default seriesColor(0))

forms.name: rank-slope
forms.question: How does the ranking reorder between two contexts?
forms.whenToUse: Re-ranking between exactly two contexts (two benchmarks, two dates, before/after) where crossings and spread change are the message.
forms.antiUse: More than two contexts — use lines; when only the gap per item matters — use dumbbell-range.
forms.props: left: string; right: string; items: {label, from, to, color?}[]; unit?='%'; height?

forms.name: share-strip
forms.question: What makes up the whole, in one strip?
forms.whenToUse: Flat part-to-whole composition of a handful of categories where the single-strip proportion is the message.
forms.antiUse: Hierarchies or many small categories — use treemap; comparing composition across subjects — use verdict-stack.

forms.name: stacked-activity
forms.question: What makes up each day's volume, and how does it breathe day to day?
forms.whenToUse: Daily volume split into 2-4 additive parts over weeks of data, where per-day composition matters as much as the trend.
forms.antiUse: Comparing exact values of individual segments across days (inner segments have no common baseline) or fewer than 5 days.
forms.props: days: ISO date strings; segments: {key,label,color,values[]} bottom-up; unit?; note?; partialLast?; partialNote?

forms.name: treemap
forms.question: How is the whole split up, and who dominates?
forms.whenToUse: Showing one full field at a glance where a few players clearly dominate — market share, install base, budget split — with roughly 5-15 items.
forms.antiUse: Not for close values (areas are hard to compare precisely) or deep hierarchies (flat only) — use rank bars or a nested treemap library instead.
forms.props: items: {label, value, valueLabel?, sub?, href?, iconUrl?, badge?, color?, muted?}[]; rows? (default 2); rowHeight? (default 96); defaultColor? (default seriesColor(0))

forms.name: value-columns
forms.question: How do these few values stack up side by side?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing one magnitude across a handful of named entities where side-by-side height reads instantly (tariffs, prices, counters).
forms.antiUse: Not for many items (>8) or time series — use rank bars or lines instead.
forms.props: items: {label, value, valueLabel?, sub?, highlight?, color?}[]; height? (default 180); maxValue?; highlightColor? (default seriesColor(0))

forms.name: verdict-stack
forms.question: What do each subject's outcomes consist of?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing the composition of outcomes or verdicts across subjects with a shared taxonomy (failure modes, ticket categories).
forms.antiUse: Reading exact segment values (no common baseline) — use a table; time series — use stacked-activity.
forms.props: subjects: {label, n, counts: Record<string, number>}[]; taxonomy: {group: string, tags: {key, label, color?}[]}[]
